alignments.note: The ASV writes As for before a fronted topic noun that carries no object marker and no preposition, so no morpheme licenses the expression and it is its own added unit headed on as (rule 16). Rule 33 is expressly unavailable here, since a topicalized nominal's fronting is not a case-function; folding the words into הֵיכָל is the reading rule 16 forecloses. The absence of an ASV italic is not evidence against it (rule 7).
The fronted topic noun takes only its own English word (rule 16).
מְזוּזָה rendered the door posts, the supplied the belonging to the nominal expression (rule 15); head on posts, which carries the lexeme.
Predicate carrying the construction-supplied copula (rule 20); head on squared.
Second supplied as for, standing before a bare construct noun with no marker and no preposition on it; added under rule 16 on the same terms as t001–t002, headed on as.
Construct noun with a supplied the; the rectum's article takes the the standing before its own word (rule 29).
Italic thereof supplies a possessive with no suffix morpheme present (rules 18, 30).
Prepositional predicate carrying the supplied copula, headed on as (rule 49).

Italic of the temple completes the ASV's comparison; the Hebrew writes only הַמַּרְאֶה and no morpheme licenses these words (rule 30). The margin's 'as the former appearance' shows the phrase is the translators' supply.

review_notes: As for at t001–t002 and t011–t012 is added under rule 16: neither fronted phrase carries an object marker or a preposition, and rule 16 names rule 33 as unavailable for a topicalized nominal. The earlier reading, which gave the words to הֵיכָל and to פְנֵי, is the one that rule forecloses.
Every other unit is as the verse pass returned it. The verse now has four added units and no unrepresented ones; all 13 source and 27 target ids are partitioned once.
